readings.title: The handover board
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: The night team at a parcel depot once left long handwritten reports for the morning team. Important unfinished jobs were often buried among routine details. A supervisor introduced a board with three columns: completed work, unresolved issues and the next required action. Each unresolved issue also named a responsible person. Reports became shorter, but the change was not simply a reduction in writing. Workers now had to decide what the next team needed to act on. After an initial week of discussion, fewer parcels were processed twice. The supervisor retained a separate log for details needed in later investigations.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: Lights along the canal
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A maintenance crew inspected canal lights after midnight because faults were easier to see in darkness. Their manager initially compared teams by the number of lamps repaired. One crew appeared slow, yet residents along its route made fewer repeat complaints. The crew leader explained that his staff checked the wiring around each failed lamp instead of replacing only the visible part. The manager added repeat faults to the monthly report and allowed extra time for diagnosis. Repair totals still mattered, but they no longer stood alone. Measuring the immediate output had overlooked whether the same problem would soon return.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: Learning at an unusual hour
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: When an adult college offered recorded lectures, many night workers watched them during breaks. Their quiz scores improved, but several still felt disconnected from classmates. The college added a discussion board where a tutor answered questions each morning. It also scheduled one live meeting at alternating times, so no group always carried the inconvenience. A warehouse worker said the recordings gave him access to information, while the discussions helped him discover what he had misunderstood. The college learned that flexible delivery solved one problem but did not automatically create a complete learning experience.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: The bakery's quiet hour
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A bakery supplying early trains asked employees to suggest changes to its overnight routine. Several proposed a quiet hour without nonessential calls. Orders would still arrive on screen, and urgent messages could reach the shift leader. During a three-week trial, packers said they made fewer counting mistakes because they were interrupted less often. However, a driver missed an update when he assumed every call was prohibited. The bakery clarified the urgent-message route and displayed it beside the phone. The trial succeeded only after the boundary between a useful interruption and an avoidable one became clear.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

translation.stem:
Translate this original passage into Chinese.

Cities continue to depend on human attention when most residents are asleep. Clean platforms, fresh bread and reliable deliveries often result from work that is rarely noticed. Recognising these contributions means more than offering praise. It also requires clear communication between shifts and schedules that allow workers to participate in family and educational life.
translation.referenceAnswer: 多数居民入睡时，城市仍然依赖人的细心工作。干净的站台、新鲜的面包和可靠的配送，往往来自很少受到关注的劳动。认可这些贡献不只是口头赞扬，还需要班次之间清晰的沟通，以及让劳动者能够参与家庭生活和教育活动的时间安排。
translation.explanation: 参考译文展示一种可接受的表达；保留原文信息及逻辑、中文通顺的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write about 120 English words for this original simulation task.

You study with classmates who work different shifts. Propose a fair group-project arrangement, explaining how to share work, exchange updates and handle a missed meeting.
writing.sampleAnswer: Our project group should begin by collecting everyone's available hours. We can divide the research into independent sections, with each member choosing a realistic deadline. A shared document should record findings, sources and questions so that progress is visible even when we cannot meet together. Short live meetings can rotate between afternoon and evening instead of always favouring the same members. After each meeting, one person should post decisions and assigned actions. Anyone who misses a meeting can add comments within the following day. If a deadline becomes difficult, the member should tell the group early so we can adjust the work. Fair participation means a dependable contribution, not attendance at every conversation.
writing.explanation: 范文用于作答后参考；观点与例子可以不同，但须回应全部要求并表达清楚。
